Porting catchmentACS workflows to v0.4

Source: vignettes/porting-v03-to-v04.qmd

This guide collects the four changes you need to know when moving a v0.3 workflow to v0.4. v0.4 is an adoption-readiness patch release: it polishes the existing v0.3 surface so that a first-time user finds it “just works.” Every v0.3 script continues to run on v0.4 without modification.

library(catchmentACS)
library(dplyr)

About the code in this article

The chunks below are illustrative and not executed (they assume Census, OSRM, or ORS access and are marked non-evaluated). The one chunk that runs only attaches the package; it makes no network calls, so this article renders fully offline. Copy a snippet into a live session to reproduce it.

Quick map

Area v0.3 behavior v0.4 change
cacs_capture_conditions() capturing a <- assignment silent footgun (assignment lost) new return_value = "both" argument
OSRM default res on the demo server 70L, prone to HTTP 429 aborts 30L plus a once-per-session migration notice
cacs_run(output = "list_column") $isochrone on the bypass path NULL populated from precomputed_isochrones
summary(run_result)$rates_breakdown mean values silently shifted (latent v0.2/v0.3 bug) corrected
as_tibble(run_result) row order underlying long-output order (rates not lifted) rate rows first within each site block
print(run_result) rates preview “Top-3 rates” (mean ± MOE) “Top 5 rates (cross-site mean ± sd)” plus a per-site mini-block
summary(run_result) slots cross-site only adds rates_per_site and rates_per_site_moe, keyed by site and drive time
cacs_summary_as_markdown() per-site shape not supported (manual pivot) shape-detected, with caption
OSRM endpoint pre-flight not present new exported cacs_validate_osrm_endpoint() helper

Issue 001 — Capturing both the result and the conditions

In v0.3 the pattern cacs_capture_conditions(acs <- cacs_acs_prefetch(...)) was a silent footgun: the <- assignment never propagated to the caller’s environment, so acs was lost. v0.4 offers two fixes.

Recommended (v0.4): return_value = "both" 

out <- cacs_capture_conditions(
  cacs_acs_prefetch(state = "AL", year = 2023),
  return_value = "both"
)
acs <- out$result        # the prefetch output
nrow(out$conditions)     # how many water-tract messages were emitted

Still valid (v0.3-compatible): <<- super-assignment 

acs <- NULL
captured <- cacs_capture_conditions(
  acs <<- cacs_acs_prefetch(state = "AL", year = 2023)
)

The v0.4 default is "conditions" (the v0.3 behavior). To switch session-wide, set options(catchmentACS.capture_return_value = "both").

Issue 002 — OSRM demo-safe default

In v0.3, cacs_isochrone(sites_sf, 10L, "osrm") with res omitted often resolved to res = 70L on the demo server, which frequently triggered an HTTP 429 quota-exhaustion abort.

In v0.4, when osrm_mode = "demo" (the default) and res is omitted, the call auto-downgrades to res = 30L and emits a once-per-session classed message. This lowers public-demo quota pressure, but depending on the endpoint’s state you may still hit a 429 or a transient failure.

# v0.4 default: 30L on demo (lower public-demo quota pressure), 70L on docker.
iso <- cacs_isochrone(sites_sf, 10L, "osrm")  # demo by default -> res = 30L

# Need the v0.3 res = 70L polygon quality? Request it explicitly:
iso_hi <- cacs_isochrone(sites_sf, 10L, "osrm", res = 70L)

# Or use a local OSRM container (no quota cost):
iso_dk <- cacs_isochrone(sites_sf, 10L, "osrm", osrm_mode = "docker")  # 70L

Pre-flight quota probe (new) 

state <- cacs_validate_osrm_endpoint()
if (state$quota_ok) {
  iso <- cacs_isochrone(sites_sf, 10L, "osrm")
} else if (identical(state$http_status, 429L)) {
  message("OSRM demo saturated; switching to docker.")
  iso <- cacs_isochrone(sites_sf, 10L, "osrm", osrm_mode = "docker")
} else {
  message("OSRM probe inconclusive or unavailable; inspect state$http_status.")
}

For the public routing.openstreetmap.de demo server, the pre-flight helper uses the profile-prefixed public-demo route path, e.g. /routed-car/route/v1/driving/.... Self-hosted OSRM endpoints keep the standard /route/v1/driving/... probe path. The returned endpoint column is the configured base server, not the internally expanded probe URL.

Disable the auto-downgrade 

options(catchmentACS.osrm_demo_budget_protect = FALSE)
iso <- cacs_isochrone(sites_sf, 10L, "osrm")  # back to v0.3 res = 70L behavior

Issue 003 — Self-contained list-column output

In v0.3, cacs_run(output = "list_column", precomputed_isochrones = iso, ...) left the $isochrone list-column as NULL, so you had to carry the isochrone object separately to visualize it.

In v0.4 the bypass path fills $isochrone automatically with the per-site sf row from precomputed_isochrones; the v0.3 manual-fill workaround is no longer needed.

run_lc <- cacs_run(
  sites = sites_sf, ...,
  precomputed_isochrones = iso,
  output = "list_column"
)
# v0.4: run_lc$isochrone[[1]] is now an sf row, not NULL.
print(run_lc$isochrone[[1]])  # visualize directly

v0.5 extends the same $isochrone fill to the computed five-call path and the four-call-B path (acs supplied, isochrones computed). As a result, output = "list_column" and output = "both" both carry the isochrone row needed for visualization, on the precomputed and computed paths alike.

Issue 004 — Per-site rate matrix on all four surfaces

In v0.3 the most important deliverable — the site × rate matrix — was hidden on all four S3 surfaces:

  • print(run_result): only a cross-site “Top 5 rates (cross-site mean ± sd)”.
  • summary(run_result): only the cross-site $rates_breakdown.
  • as_tibble(run_result): rate rows trailed behind the source ACS rows.
  • cacs_summary_as_markdown(): cross-site shape only.

v0.4 exposes the per-site, per-drive-time matrix on all four surfaces, within zero clicks. A single internal helper is the single source of truth.

Track 1 — summary() slots and the breakdown argument 

sm <- summary(run_result)
sm$rates_per_site         # tibble [n_keys x (key columns + 5)] — numeric
sm$rates_per_site_moe     # same key shape, with "x +/- y" strings
# Key columns are site_id and, when available, drive_time_min.

# Explicit print control:
sm_b <- summary(run_result, breakdown = "both")
print(sm_b)               # cross-site and per-site together

Track 2 — print() mini-block

print(run_result) now shows a “Rates per site” mini-block automatically. The gating option is getOption("catchmentACS.summary_per_site_max", 12L) (default 12); set it to 0L to disable.

Track 3 — as_tibble() rate-first 

tbl <- tibble::as_tibble(run_result)
# v0.4 default: rate rows surface above the source ACS B-codes within each
# (site_id, drive_time_min) block.

# Disable the v0.4 rate-first lift and return the underlying long row order:
tbl_v03 <- tibble::as_tibble(run_result, rate_first = FALSE)

Track 4 — cacs_summary_as_markdown() per-site 

md <- cacs_summary_as_markdown(sm$rates_per_site)
# "## Rates per site (estimate)" plus a pipe-Markdown table for Quarto/paper.

md_moe <- cacs_summary_as_markdown(sm$rates_per_site_moe)
# "## Rates per site (estimate +/- 90% MOE)" with "x +/- y" cells.

Latent v0.2/v0.3 correctness fix

A cross-surface invariant test added in v0.4 surfaced a silent correctness bug present in v0.2 and v0.3:

  • The summary(run_result)$rates_breakdown$mean values were circularly shifted: each rate row’s reported mean was actually the value belonging to the next alphabetical position.
  • Cause: the cacs_run_result S3 class interfered with the group-key alignment in dplyr’s group_by() + summarise().
  • v0.4 fix: internal aggregation uses a plain-tibble helper before dplyr, and dplyr::group_by(cacs_run_result, ...) now strips the presentation class before constructing the grouped data frame.

Action required for v0.3 users: any rates_breakdown mean values you have already published or shared should be re-computed and verified against a v0.4 build.

What did not change

  • The execution-path semantics of cacs_run() (five-call / three-call / four-call).
  • The 14 entries in cacs_acs_default_vars and the 5 rates in cacs_acs_default_rates.
  • The cacs_intersect_weight(keep_tract_audit = TRUE) attribute.
  • The issue-table contract of cacs_validate_iso().
  • The five-method dispatch of cacs_describe().
  • Every sanctioned v0.3 rate formula (in particular ssi_rate = B19056_002 / B19056_001).
  • The cache-fingerprint sidecar contract.
